title: Keyboard Manager: Duplicate output on shortcut

status.label: Reproduce duplicate Send Text output from Pause
status.detail: The report gives an exact Shift+Pause shortcut and Send Text action that emits the string three times; it uses PowerToys 0.96.0.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a specific shortcut (Left Shift+Pause) mapped to a Send Text action and says pressing it emits “npx expo start” three times, while an online keyboard tester registers one press. It lists PowerToys 0.96.0 and says the target can be VS Code or none. The source code search found no dedicated Pause-key special case in Keyboard Manager, so maintainer reproduction on current stable with an alternate trigger key will clarify whether repeats come from Pause handling or the text-action path.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.96.0 from Microsoft Store.
The mapping is Left Shift+Pause → Send Text “npx expo start”, with target app code.exe or none.
The reported output contains three consecutive copies, while the reporter says an online keyboard tester registers only one press.
The issue is open with no comments or assignees.
A repository search found no Pause-specific branch in Keyboard Manager; the symptom still needs a current controlled reproduction.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact shortcut and compare Pause with an alternate trigger key and Send Text with a non-text action on current stable.

fix_assessment.rationale: The exact report supports a maintainer reproduction, but the cause could be Pause key event behavior or repeated text-action invocation and is not isolated.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate repeated Send Text output from a Pause-key shortcut
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Pause-key shortcut may generate multiple shortcut invocations or the Send Text path may be repeated for this trigger; the report does not establish which path is responsible.
plan: Reproduce Left Shift+Pause → Send Text on v0.102.3001 with target app unset and VS Code.
Compare with the same Send Text action on a normal trigger key and with a non-text action on Pause.
If repetition is specific to Pause, trace its key-down/up event sequence; if it occurs with other triggers, trace the Send Text invocation path.
verification: Confirm one trigger produces exactly one “npx expo start” output.
Verify the target-app setting does not cause duplicate output and ordinary shortcut triggers still work.

confidence.rationale: The report is specific and distinguishes a keyboard tester result, but there is no current-build reproduction or evidence separating Pause events from text-action handling.

issue_context.summary: A Left Shift+Pause shortcut mapped to Send Text reportedly inserts “npx expo start” three times.
known_information: The shortcut is Left Shift+Pause and the action sends “npx expo start”; target app is code.exe or none.

inferences: Pause may generate a nonstandard key event sequence or the Send Text action may be invoked multiple times, but neither mechanism is established.
issue_context.analysis: Use a controlled comparison to separate source-key events from Send Text behavior. The issue is reproducible enough for a maintainer test without requesting another report or diagnostics.
